We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge 0.17).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/759e123d5c61321e78b085260a14d5ae98a54b724b82b06cdecc46ff28072b8b.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-P(Z<0.17) \\  & =1-Φ(0.17)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/83ab5f91c5ee81eeb4c31b42558af5c46cb59d74603b30913ab80dadeafc3317.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.17)=0.5675.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-Φ(0.17) \\  & =1-0.5675 \\  & =0.4325.\end{aligned}
$$
